evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/utils/session.ts:114 — buildSessionUser() builds the signed-in user from a login response by casting the server-embedded object straight through: `const user = { ...embedded } as unknown as SessionUser;`. Only `str(embedded.id)` is checked (L113); every other field (role/email/firstName/lastName) is trusted as-is across the API trust boundary.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/utils/session.ts:16,29 — SessionUser.role is the strict union `AppRole = 'owner' | 'tenant' | 'resident' | 'manager' | 'admin'`. The embedded path does NOT normalize role, whereas the claims-fallback path does: L128 `role: toAppRole(str(claims.role) ?? active?.role)`. toAppRole (L72) maps backend roles `property_manager`/`technical_manager` -> 'manager', `owner_delegate` -> 'owner', default -> 'resident'.

Consequence: when the server embeds a raw backend role string in `data.user.role`, user.role keeps an un-mapped value that is not a valid AppRole, so role-gated UI (e.g. `role === 'manager'`) silently misclassifies the user and shows the wrong navigation/permissions. The two code paths that build the same SessionUser disagree on role normalization. Fix vector (cloud-landable, TS-only): run the embedded role through toAppRole() and validate string fields instead of a blanket `as unknown as` cast; add a session.test.ts case for an embedded backend-role payload.
